objective.statement: Compare triplets in simple time with ordinary beats of compound time.
successCriteria: I know three quavers in a compound beat need no triplet sign.
I know a triplet in 2/4 sounds like the beats of 6/8.
I can match a simple time signature with its compound partner.

explanation.text: A triplet puts three notes into a beat that is normally divided into two. Compound time works the other way round: dividing every beat into three is the normal pattern. The two can sound exactly the same.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 2/4: two beats, each a triplet of three quavers.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: a triplet of quaver, quaver, quaver, a triplet of quaver, quaver, quaver.

explanation.caption: 2/4 with a triplet on each beat. The 3 is needed to show three notes in a crotchet beat.

music.textAlternative: One bar of 6/8: two beats, each three beamed quavers.
music.questionAlternative: Bar 1: 3 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver), 3 beamed together (quaver, quaver, quaver).

explanation.caption: 6/8 with three quavers on each beat. No sign is needed.

explanation.text: Both bars have two beats and six even quavers. They are written differently, and that difference matters: in 2/4 the beat is a crotchet, in 6/8 it is a dotted crotchet.
Each simple time signature with triplets has a compound partner with the same number of beats: 2/4 and 6/8 (two beats), 3/4 and 9/8 (three beats), 4/4 and 12/8 (four beats).
Triplet in simple time: needs a 3. Compound time: three in a beat is already the rule.

steps: Tap a bar of 2/4 with a triplet on each beat: six even notes.
Tap a bar of 6/8 with three quavers on each of two beats: the same six even notes.
The sound is the same. Only the way it is written differs.

guided.prompt: This bar is in 9/8. Does the group of three beamed quavers in the first beat need a triplet sign (a 3)?

options.label: Yes, it needs a 3 over the three quavers

yes.reason: 9/8 is compound time: every beat is a dotted crotchet that already divides into three quavers. No sign is needed for that.

hints: Compound time: the beat already divides into three. Simple time: three in a beat is a triplet.
Compound time: the beat divides into three without any sign.

feedback.correct: Yes: you decided from the kind of time.

mistakes.tuplet-total-wrong: A tuplet still fills a fixed amount of time. Check which beat it replaces.
mistakes.tuplet-number-wrong: Count the notes that share the beat — that's the number to write over the group.
mistakes.written-value-wrong: Use the note value the group would have if it divided normally — then add the tuplet number.
mistakes.simple-compound-confusion: Count the equal parts in each beat: two means simple time, three means compound time.
mistakes.tuplet-ignored: A triplet puts three notes into one ordinary beat, so count three notes for that beat.
mistakes.beat-count-wrong: Count the beats in a bar: in simple time the top number counts them; in 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8 the top number counts quavers, so divide it by three.
mistakes.beat-unit-wrong: Check which note is one beat. In simple time the bottom number names it. In 6/8, 9/8 and 12/8 the beat is a dotted note holding three of the notes the bottom number names, so the bottom number alone does not name it.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Ask: how many notes, in the time of how many?
